Why the other options are wrong:
• CloudTrail management events only: Management events do not include object reads.
• S3 Storage Lens usage dashboards: Storage Lens shows usage.
• S3 Inventory reports by prefix: Inventory lists objects.

Key takeaway: Audit object access with CloudTrail data events.

stem: A company must retain and query audit logs of Redshift user activity and connections. Which TWO features help? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Redshift concurrency scaling configuration
Redshift audit logging to S3 or CloudWatch Logs
Redshift Spectrum external schema setup
Redshift snapshots taken every eight hours
System tables and views for query history

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Audit logging captures connection and user activity, and system tables record queries.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Redshift concurrency scaling configuration: Concurrency scaling adds capacity.
• Redshift Spectrum external schema setup: Spectrum queries S3.
• Redshift snapshots taken every eight hours: Snapshots back up data.

Key takeaway: Audit Redshift with audit logs and system tables.

stem: A company wants to query a year of CloudTrail logs across accounts with SQL. Which TWO options fit? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Route 53 query logging
S3 Inventory reports only
Athena on CloudTrail logs in S3
EC2 console output logs
CloudTrail Lake queries

explanation:
Why this is correct:
CloudTrail Lake and Athena both provide SQL over CloudTrail data.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Route 53 query logging: DNS logs are unrelated.
• S3 Inventory reports only: Inventory lists objects.
• EC2 console output logs: Console output logs are unrelated.

Key takeaway: SQL over audit logs → CloudTrail Lake or Athena.

stem: A company must find S3 objects containing personal data across many buckets. Which service fits?

choices.text: AWS WAF
Amazon Inspector
Amazon Macie
AWS Shield

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Macie discovers sensitive data such as PII in S3.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS WAF: WAF filters web requests.
• Amazon Inspector: Inspector scans vulnerabilities.
• AWS Shield: Shield protects against DDoS.

Key takeaway: Discover PII in S3 → Macie.

stem: Regulations require customer data to remain in the EU. Which TWO controls help? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Storing and processing data only in EU Regions
Using global tables across every AWS Region
Replicating data to all Regions for resilience
Sending data to a US Region for analytics jobs
SCPs denying actions outside approved EU Regions

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Region-restricting SCPs and EU-only storage and processing enforce residency.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Using global tables across every AWS Region: Global tables replicate outside the EU.
• Replicating data to all Regions for resilience: Replication everywhere breaks residency.
• Sending data to a US Region for analytics jobs: US processing breaks residency.

Key takeaway: Enforce data residency with Region controls.

stem: A company must share a dataset with a partner account securely without copying it, with governance. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Making the S3 bucket public for the partner's convenience
Lake Formation cross-account sharing or Redshift data sharing
Emailing the dataset as a spreadsheet to the partner
Giving the partner the company's IAM user credentials

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Governed sharing mechanisms grant access without copying or exposing credentials.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Making the S3 bucket public for the…: Public buckets expose data.
• Emailing the dataset as a spreadsheet to the…: Email is insecure and ungoverned.
• Giving the partner the company's IAM user…: Sharing credentials is insecure.

Key takeaway: Share data with governed, cross-account mechanisms.

stem: A governance team wants to classify datasets by sensitivity and require approval before analysts can subscribe to sensitive data. Which service fits?

choices.text: Amazon CloudWatch dashboards that display each dataset's usage
Amazon SES email templates for approvals
AWS Batch job definitions for each dataset
Amazon DataZone (SageMaker Catalog) with subscription approvals

explanation:
Why this is correct:
DataZone supports publishing, classification metadata, and approval workflows for data access.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Amazon CloudWatch dashboards that display…: Dashboards do not govern access.
• Amazon SES email templates for approvals: Email templates do not enforce approvals.
• AWS Batch job definitions for each dataset: Batch runs jobs.

Key takeaway: Govern data subscriptions with DataZone.

stem: Personal data must be removed or pseudonymized before loading into an analytics environment. Which step fits?

choices.text: Loading raw data and asking analysts not to look at PII
A transformation that masks or tokenizes PII fields before loading
Encrypting the analytics bucket and sharing the key widely
Removing all data older than one day to limit exposure

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Masking or tokenizing PII before loading reduces exposure in analytics.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Loading raw data and asking analysts not to…: Instructions do not protect data.
• Encrypting the analytics bucket and sharing…: Shared keys defeat encryption.
• Removing all data older than one day to…: Deleting data does not address PII.

Key takeaway: Pseudonymize PII before analytics.

stem: EMR clusters must authenticate users with Kerberos and integrate with the corporate directory. Which feature fits?

choices.text: EMR managed scaling policies tied to directory groups
EMR bootstrap actions only
EMR security configuration with Kerberos authentication
EMR instance fleet settings

explanation:
Why this is correct:
EMR security configurations enable Kerberos authentication, including cross-realm trust.

Why the other options are wrong:
• EMR managed scaling policies tied to…: Scaling adjusts capacity.
• EMR bootstrap actions only: Bootstrap actions run scripts.
• EMR instance fleet settings: Instance fleets choose instance types.

Key takeaway: EMR user authentication → Kerberos security configuration.

stem: Which TWO measures apply least privilege to a data pipeline's IAM roles? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Allow s3:* on all resources for flexibility
Share one role across every team and pipeline
Attach AdministratorAccess to simplify operations
Scope S3 permissions to specific buckets and prefixes
Use separate roles for separate pipeline stages

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Scoped permissions and per-stage roles limit access to what each step needs.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Allow s3:* on all resources for flexibility: Wildcards grant excess access.
• Share one role across every team and pipeline: Shared roles grant excess access.
• Attach AdministratorAccess to simplify…: Admin access violates least privilege.

Key takeaway: Scope and separate pipeline roles.

stem: A daily batch must join 5 TB of S3 data with a dimension table and write results as Parquet. Which serverless option fits with minimal operations?

choices.text: An AWS Glue Spark job
A manual Athena console run
An RDS stored procedure
A single Lambda function

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Glue Spark jobs process large joins serverlessly and write Parquet.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A manual Athena console run: Manual runs are not automated.
• An RDS stored procedure: RDS is not suited for 5 TB S3 processing.
• A single Lambda function: Lambda limits make 5 TB joins impractical.

Key takeaway: Large serverless joins → Glue Spark.

stem: A pipeline must pause until a data steward approves a new dataset before loading it. Which Step Functions feature fits?

choices.text: A Pass state that forwards its input directly
A Wait state set to a fixed number of hours
A Map state processing all items in parallel
A task token callback waiting for approval

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Callback tasks with task tokens pause until an external approval returns the token.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A Pass state that forwards its input directly: Pass forwards input.
• A Wait state set to a fixed number of hours: Fixed waits do not reflect approval.
• A Map state processing all items in parallel: Map runs iterations.

Key takeaway: Human approval in workflows → task tokens.

stem: A Glue crawler updates table schemas automatically, but a recent change broke downstream queries. Which setting prevents unwanted schema changes?

choices.text: Configure the crawler to ignore changes or only add new columns, and review changes
Grant analysts permission to edit the table schema by hand daily
Run the crawler more often so that any broken schemas are replaced by newer ones faster
Delete the Data Catalog table after each crawler run completes

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Crawler schema change policies control how updates are applied, preventing breaking changes.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Grant analysts permission to edit the table…: Manual edits are error-prone.
• Run the crawler more often so that any…: More runs spread breaking changes faster.
• Delete the Data Catalog table after each…: Deleting tables breaks queries.

Key takeaway: Control crawler schema updates with change policies.
